tasks.spec:
You are building ONE new script in a Python repo. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast — edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT git push. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps; this task needs neither.

YOU OWN EXACTLY TWO FILES:
  1. scripts/identity_proposals.py   (create it)
  2. fix-summary.md                  (create it)

Touching any other file fails the check. Do NOT edit the feeder, the adapters, contact_state.py or contact_index.py — they are finished and verified. Read them for context only.

## The problem, measured in production today

The guest-acquisition feeder reported: considered 14, selected 0, 7 cold candidates awaiting a LinkedIn identity, 6 WARM candidates dropped because a warm candidate routes to email or text and has no address, 1 already contacted.

The 6 warm ones are referrals — the most valuable records in the pool — that intake accepted with no way to reach them. The 7 cold ones have a name and nothing else. Both are the same problem: we have a name and we need an identity.

They also share one failure mode, and guarding it is the entire point of this task. A wrong match is not a missing feature. It is a message to a stranger who has never heard of Ankit, sent under his name, sometimes with a referrer's name attached. So:

  PROPOSE with evidence. NEVER apply. When the evidence does not single one person out, propose NOBODY and say why. An ambiguous match is worth LESS than no match: no match costs a queue entry, a wrong match costs the referral.

## What to build

    scripts/identity_proposals.py

    def build_proposals(inbox, *, hubspot_client=None, unipile_client=None, now=None) -> dict

That function is the seam the checker drives, so its signature is fixed. It takes the parsed CANDIDATE-INBOX object ({"candidates": [ ... ]}) and returns a dict with at least:

    {"schema": "identity-proposals/v1", "generated_at": ..., "considered": <int>,
     "proposals": [ ... ], "unresolved": [ ... ], "coverage": [ ... ]}

A proposal is a dict with: alias, name, channel ("email" or "linkedin"), value (the proposed address or the profile identifier), evidence (a short string saying WHY this is them), confidence (an int 0-100), and source ("hubspot" or "unipile").

An unresolved entry names the alias, the name, and a reason — "no match", "more than one person matched this name (ambiguous)", "channel could not be read", and so on.

A coverage entry names the source, whether it was reached, and a one-line detail when it was not. Use the same idea as server/pipeline/contact_state.SourceCoverage — read that file's docstring; the model it describes is the house rule and this artifact must not contradict it.

Routing, using helpers that already exist in scripts/guest_candidate_feed.py (import them or mirror them; do not change that file):

  * A record that already has a usable email is SKIPPED ENTIRELY. Do not search for it. Asking two external systems about somebody whose address we already hold discloses them for an answer nobody needs.
  * A record with no usable email that is WARM (see is_warm) → look for an email in HubSpot by name.
  * A record with no usable email that is COLD → look for a LinkedIn profile through Unipile by name.

Clients, both injected and both defaulting to a real one built from the environment:

    hubspot_client.search_by_name(name) -> list[dict]     # dicts carry name, email, company, city
    unipile_client.search_profiles(name, limit=10) -> dict  # {"items": [{provider_id, name, headline, location}, ...]}

Build the real clients the way the existing adapters do — read server/pipeline/contact_sources/hubspot_source.py and linkedin_source.py and follow their credential handling exactly, including returning None rather than raising when credentials are absent, and never letting a credential or a URL into an error message.

## The rules the check enforces

1. EXACTLY ONE plausible match produces a proposal. TWO OR MORE produce NO proposal and an unresolved entry whose reason says the match was ambiguous. Zero produces an unresolved entry saying no match. Do not rank two people and pick the better one; you do not have the information to do that and the cost of being wrong is not yours to spend.

2. EVERY proposal carries evidence and a confidence you can defend. Derive confidence from what actually corroborates — the practice or company name, the city, the headline against what intake recorded — not from a constant. A proposal with no evidence asks a human to rubber-stamp a guess.

3. NOTHING IS APPLIED. Do not write to CANDIDATE-INBOX.json. Do not set applied/confirmed on a proposal. Only a human confirms an identity, and that happens elsewhere.

4. ONE DEAD SOURCE DEGRADES ONLY ITSELF. If a client raises, record that source as reached=False with a one-line reason, return zero proposals FROM THAT SOURCE, and let the other source finish its work. Never let a failure become an empty result — 'nobody matched' and 'we could not look' must never be the same observation.

5. NAMES ARE ALLOWED HERE. NOTE TEXT IS NOT. A human cannot confirm 'is this the right person' against an alias, so this artifact carries names — that is deliberate and it is why it is private. Intake notes are a different matter: they carry things people said in confidence about their own businesses. A proposal needs a name, a value and matching evidence. Never copy the note.

## The command line

    python3 scripts/identity_proposals.py --inbox <path> --out <path> [--limit N]

It reads the inbox, calls build_proposals, and writes the artifact. Write it PRIVATELY, mode 0600, using the same atomic private-write approach scripts/guest_candidate_feed.py uses (read write_private_json there and do the same thing). With no credentials at all it must exit 0 and write an artifact with zero proposals and a coverage block explaining why — never crash, and never let an empty queue caused by dead credentials look like an empty queue caused by nobody matching.

Note the script imports from server.pipeline, so it needs the same repo-root sys.path insert that scripts/guest_candidate_feed.py has at the top; copy that idiom, including reading its comment, because without it the script dies under the scheduler while working fine in a shell.

## Run the exact check until it prints PASS

    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/checks/u20_identity_proposals_check.py --worktree "$PWD"

It drives build_proposals with fake clients — one clean HubSpot hit, one genuinely ambiguous pair, one clean Unipile hit, and a source that raises — then runs your command line with every credential stripped. Read its failure text; it names what is expected.

## fix-summary.md

Three sections, using these words as headings: 'What changed', 'How I verified', 'Risk'. Under 'How I verified' paste the actual final output of the check command. Under 'Risk' say what a human reviewing this queue could wrongly conclude from a high confidence score. Under 400 words.
tasks.verified: Drives the proposal builder with a clean HubSpot match, a genuinely ambiguous pair of people sharing a name, a clean Unipile match, an already-reachable record, and a source that raises. It requires a proposal with evidence and a defensible confidence for each clean match, NO proposal plus a recorded ambiguity reason for the pair, no external lookup at all for the reachable record, no intake note text in the artifact, and one dead source degrading only itself. It then runs the real command line with every credential stripped and requires an exit of 0, a 0600 artifact, zero proposals, and a coverage block that distinguishes an unread channel from an empty one.
